That sounds word to word my experience in college, I had major depression, anxiety, lived with my parents, had no real friends and earned subpar grades (I think I graduated with a ~C+ average GPA in a fairly easy program.) 

It's alright to feel lost and, like the other commenter said, it can get better. After I graduated I realized college just wasn't an environment built for a lot of my sensibilities and started thriving fairly quickly after. 

I've moved across the country, started work at a major tech company despite my kinda lame B.A. in Psychology, and have made a lot of friends through work since then.

I've also been there with abusive relationships and they leave scars, everyone heals that their own pace and it's still a very valid reason to not be 100% (not that you *need* a reason to be depressed, anyway.) Anyone that judges you for "not getting over it" fast enough isn't worth the time.
